query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

decision.trend: The trend in the research on high-entropy alloys is towards developing new methods and models to improve the representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid. Recent studies have focused on using advanced ab initio-based techniques, such as Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflows and deep learning potentials, to explore Pareto-optimal compositions and predict material properties. The use of these methods has led to improved predictions of melting temperatures and thermodynamic properties, and has provided insights into the trade-off relationships between competing properties.
decision.unsolved: The inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid remains a significant challenge. The development of new methods and models that can accurately capture the complex behavior of high-entropy alloys is an active area of research.
decision.why: The use of deep learning potentials has shown promise in improving the prediction of material properties, such as melting temperatures, and has the potential to overcome the limitations of EAM references. By developing and applying deep learning potentials to high-entropy alloys, researchers may be able to improve the representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid and gain a better understanding of the thermodynamic properties of these materials.
